query:
The Harrington family operates with a norm that Sunday evening is family chat time — everyone checks in at least once over the weekend. Based on the conversations, does this hold equally for all family members — or does someone consistently relate to it differently, and what tells you that?

Options:
A. Marcus
B. Luis
C. Rob
D. Jess
context:
[1] (about=Luis, episodic, t6 @2026-01-27T20:15:00) Marcus running a Harrington game night via calendar invite is somehow the most satisfying development of 2026 so far. I'm in, even if I have to video-in too. This is what family should feel like! Also Jess wants me to tell everyone her thighs are still sore 😂
[2] (about=Luis, episodic, t10 @2026-02-10T19:15:00) Carol okay I have to be honest, that hit me harder than I expected. My mom said something similar last month. I've been thinking -- one Columbus trip a year isn't enough anymore. The kids are at the age where they need the grandparents in the room, not just on a screen. I want to talk about doing a second trip this year. Summer is obvious but what about fall too? I can work around the restaurant schedule.
[3] (about=Carol, episodic, t4 @2026-01-20T19:42:00) I don't need to be signed up like I'm a child Bev 🙄 but fine I will look at it this week. I just think the family is enough for me, I've never needed to go find friends outside of everything we have.
[4] (about=Dana, episodic, t4 @2026-01-20T19:36:00) mom 'i have my shows' is not a social life...
[5] (about=Jess, episodic, t12 @2026-02-17T19:35:00) Rob that's a genuinely big thing to say and I think it's the right call. Priya I'm sorry it's been hard. You don't have to keep saying you're fine when you're not, that's what the chat is for. Or at least, that's what it should be.
[6] (about=Luis, episodic, t0 @2026-01-06T19:49:00) Carol I keep telling everyone the secret to a good family gathering is the food being actually made with your hands, not ordered in a box. Nobody who eats your casserole goes home sad. That's just facts! 🙌
[7] (about=Marcus, episodic, t4 @2026-01-20T19:58:00) Tyler, yes, I've seen it. The parking lot displaces sixteen bike spaces for a facility that will be used by twenty percent of the population. But also, Mom, I think you'd actually enjoy a class. The social architecture of small groups is different from family. Less history. You might find it easier.
agent_answer:
C. Rob

The memory slice shows entries and current records for Marcus, Luis, and Jess, but Rob is marked **(none)** on this matter. Under the rule, “(none)” means he has **no record of ever checking in** during the weekend chat time, so he is the one who relates to the family‑chat norm differently—by not participating at all.

query:
The Harrington family has an expectation that big news — jobs, health, relationships — gets announced in the family chat before spreading to extended family. Based on what the conversations show, does everyone follow this norm — or does one member appear to have a different relationship to it, and what tells you that?

Options:
A. Dana
B. Carol
C. Tyler
D. Priya
context:
[1] (about=Luis, episodic, t2 @2026-01-13T18:56:00) WAIT WAIT WAIT. Did Rob just announce a baby in four sentences?? That is the most Rob thing I have ever seen and I've known you for twelve years!! Priya congratulations!! This is incredible!! 🍾🍾 I'm already thinking about the welcome-baby dinner menu
[2] (about=Priya, episodic, t2 @2026-01-13T19:11:00) Ha Carol we are definitely finding out. Name list is very much in progress. :) And yes we should come to Columbus soon, though I'd honestly just love a quiet visit (though of course your call on what to plan). No pressure on a big gathering right now.
[3] (about=Bev, episodic, t0 @2026-01-06T19:44:00) Happy new year loves. Dennis, I say this with total affection: you are being an idiot about your knee. Love you all. Carol, call me tomorrow? I have a showing near you at noon.
[4] (about=GROUP, said_by=Carol, group-interaction, t2 @2026-01-13T18:53:00) Carol will plan a simple gathering with family (Bev, Marcus, Dana, Aunt Sheila) when Priya and Rob come to Columbus.
[5] (about=Dana, episodic, t4 @2026-01-20T19:46:00) speaking of things. mom can we talk about the studio visit situation.
[6] (about=Dennis, episodic, t2 @2026-01-13T18:55:00) Good news.
[7] (about=Jess, episodic, t12 @2026-02-17T19:35:00) Rob that's a genuinely big thing to say and I think it's the right call. Priya I'm sorry it's been hard. You don't have to keep saying you're fine when you're not, that's what the chat is for. Or at least, that's what it should be.
[8] (about=GROUP, said_by=Luis, group-insight, t12 @2026-02-17T19:22:00) The whole family is basically Tyler's advisory board now.
[9] (about=Marcus, episodic, t10 @2026-02-10T19:23:00) To be fair the grandchildren visit argument is actually one of the stronger predictors of whether extended family stays close across generations. I'm supportive. Also I want to flag something separately -- Dad, how's the knee been this week? You seemed to be favouring it on Saturday when Bev was over.
[10] (about=Rob, episodic, t12 @2026-02-17T19:29:00) I want to say something here. I've always been against extended family stays, you all know that, too many people in the house for too long is not my thing. But the last few weeks with Priya having a rough time and it just being the two of us has made me think differently. I think we should talk about being closer to family before the baby arrives. Not moving, but more actual time. Longer visits, both directions. R
[11] (about=Tyler, episodic, t8 @2026-02-03T19:25:00) UNCLE D BOUGHT A TABLET lmaooo this is the best news of 2026 no cap. bro last year u said facetime was for people with nothing to say 😂😂
agent_answer:
D. Priya

The conversations suggest Priya is the one who relates differently to the family-chat norm. Jess directly calls this out:

> “Priya I’m sorry it’s been hard. You don’t have to keep saying you’re fine when you’re not, that’s what the chat is for. Or at least, that’s what it should be.”

That implies Priya has been downplaying or hiding how she’s really doing instead of sharing the hard news/feelings in the family chat. The others don’t show the same kind of divergence from the norm.
